outlook: Grains bounced early Tuesday on slower-than-expected harvest progress, a weaker dollar and higher crude oil, but gave it all back to close lower. December corn fell 5½ cents to about $4.61½, a two-month low, and November soybeans lost 5¼ cents to about $12.48, an eight-week low, as harvest pressure outweighed another 114,000 tonnes of confirmed soybean sales to China. Wheat led the losses on ample global supply and weak U.S. export demand: Chicago December dropped 12½ cents to about $6.43 and Minneapolis December spring wheat fell 7¾ cents to about $6.62. ICE November canola slipped C$6.50 to C$780.50 per tonne.

news.title: Grain futures rise after hitting multi-week lows on Tuesday
